stem: A client is prescribed potassium chloride extended-release tablets. Which instruction should the nurse include?

options.A: Take the tablets on an empty stomach to maximize absorption
options.B: Take the tablets with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid
options.C: Take the medication only once each week regardless of the prescribed dose
options.D: Chew the extended-release tablets thoroughly before swallowing

rationale: Current DailyMed labeling instructs that potassium chloride extended-release tablets be taken with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid and not on an empty stomach because of gastric irritation risk. Product-specific instructions should be followed for swallowing or alternative administration. B is correct.
educational_objective: Teach safe oral administration of potassium chloride extended-release tablets to reduce gastrointestinal irritation.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
source_locator: Dosage and Administration — take with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid; do not take on an empty stomach
source_claim_supported: Potassium chloride extended-release tablets should be taken with meals and liquid and should not be taken on an empty stomach because of potential gastric irritation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — oral electrolyte replacement

source_original.stem: A client is prescribed oral potassium chloride supplements. The nurse should instruct the client to:

options.A: Take the medication on an empty stomach for best absorption
options.B: Take with food or a full glass of water to reduce GI irritation
options.C: Take the medication only once per week regardless of dose
options.D: Chew extended-release tablets thoroughly before swallowing

source_original.rationale: Oral potassium chloride can cause significant GI irritation, including nausea, vomiting, and even ulceration in some cases. Taking the medication with food or a full glass of water helps reduce this irritation. Extended-release tablets/capsules should generally be swallowed whole, not chewed or crushed, unless specifically indicated otherwise.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed potassium chloride ER: take with meals and water; avoid empty stomach because of gastric irritation; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Corrected the keyed wording from 'with food OR a full glass of water' to the label-supported instruction 'with meals AND with a glass of water or other liquid.' Removed unnecessary overgeneralization about all extended-release potassium products and used a current DailyMed locator.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current official DailyMed label; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: A DailyMed potassium chloride ER label current in 2026 was checked on 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The label explicitly requires meals plus a glass of water/other liquid and warns against empty-stomach administration because of gastric irritation.

distractor_audit.C: Invented dosing frequency unrelated to the prescribed regimen.
distractor_audit.D: Unsafe/generalized manipulation instruction for an extended-release product.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B is uniquely label-concordant after changing OR to AND.
audit_findings.cueing: Choices are short, parallel administration instructions.
audit_findings.blueprint: Medication education and administration fit Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current DailyMed Dosage and Administration; the original OR wording was not acceptable and has been corrected.
